title: Overtime nearly tripled; hundreds now earn more in overtime than in salary

beats.text: Picture a City employee paid for 16.8 hours a day. Every day of the year.

visual.label: paid hours a day, every day of the year
visual.sub: one Police Department payroll record, fiscal 2026

beats.text: City overtime was 174.6 million dollars in fiscal 2014.
By fiscal 2026?
513.4 million dollars: nearly tripled, in a year with one extra pay period.

visual.label: overtime paid, fiscal 2026
visual.sub: 10.4% of salaries, up from 6.9%; fiscal 2026 had 27 pay periods, one more than usual

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: Start with that record. A Police Sergeant 3,
on a salary of 220,100 dollars. The overtime?
522,802 dollars.
That’s 6,132 paid hours.
How is that possible? Paid hours aren’t clock hours.

visual.line: leave cashed out, standby pay, time credited at premium rates

beats.text: They can include leave cashed out, standby pay, and premium-rate credits.

visual.line: leave cashed out, standby pay, time credited at premium rates

beats.text: Now count the names on the payroll paid more in overtime than in salary.
In 2014 there were 29. In 2026?

visual.label: names on the payroll paid more in overtime than in salary

beats.text: 279 names have done it in three or more years. But a name may be two people.

visual.label: names that did it in three or more years
visual.sub: the file identifies people by name since fiscal 2017

beats.text: Where is it paid? At the Sheriff’s Office, overtime equals 46 percent of base pay.

visual.label: Overtime as a share of base pay, fiscal 2026

beats.text: Police overtime alone went from 28 million dollars to 163.4 million.

visual.kicker: Police: 2.12 times its overtime budget, fiscal 2019 to 2026

beats.text: In December 2024, the Board’s Budget and Legislative Analyst audited Police overtime.

visual.label: Performance Audit of Police Dept Overtime

beats.text: It found about 51,000 ineligible overtime hours, worked by employees with high sick leave.

visual.label: ineligible 10B overtime hours, 2020 to 2023
visual.sub: worked by employees with high sick leave usage

beats.text: It found all nine overtime limits broken: 16,688 weeks over 20 overtime hours in one year.

visual.label: weeks over 20 overtime hours, fiscal 2022-23
visual.sub: all nine overtime limits broken, fiscal 2018-19 to 2022-23

beats.text: Of 559 overtime cards sampled, 18 showed a lieutenant or sergeant approving their own overtime.

visual.title: 559 overtime cards sampled
rows: A lieutenant or sergeant approving their own overtime

beats.text: One investigation of excessive overtime in five years, and no Annual Overtime Report in those years.

visual.label: One investigation in five years
visual.sub: no Annual Overtime Report in fiscal 2018-19 to 2022-23; the Controller reported overtime again in May 2026
visual.chip: 7,350 police complaint allegations: none concerns overtime

beats.text: The department agreed with 12 of 29 recommendations, and reports an overtime compliance unit.
Some overtime is built into the rules: mandatory hours pay time and a half.
In 2013, the Controller wrote that Fire overtime results from deliberate Department decisions,

visual.text: Overtime use within the department is the result of deliberate Department decisions regarding how to cost-effectively meet minimum staffing requirements

beats.text: on how to meet minimum staffing requirements cost-effectively.

visual.text: Overtime use within the department is the result of deliberate Department decisions regarding how to cost-effectively meet minimum staffing requirements

beats.text: The Fire Department’s budget says it must rely on overtime to meet staffing.

beats.text: Vacancies drive it too. Emergency Management reported 122 dispatchers in post,
against 189 authorized.
The records don’t show that any hour went unworked.
